title: The system skill
purpose: The skill turns {subject}'s sources into {contract}, one checked file from which {reader} rebuilds {subject} without the sources.

sources.says: the three cases and their order
the topics and where each finding goes
the record layout and how to write each part
the survey behind each tag's items

terms.meaning: the one JSON file that holds all that is known of {subject}; every page is drawn from it
{area} that holds the states of one thing, exactly one of them current
a static edge read as `<from> <label> <to>`, which must be true of {subject}
what {contract} lacks, forbids wrongly, says twice or says with two meanings

levels.title: system-skill
levels.about: Between {subject} and {reader}, three jobs in turn carry what the sources say into two kept files, and {contract} is fit for {reader} only in the last of its three states.

levels.title: parts-of-a-contract
levels.about: {contract} draws {subject} with four parts on each level and holds all levels together with three more.

info.why: Set apart what the skill meets and does not make.

info.exit: each open question on {contract} is answered or recorded
info.why: Order the jobs of one run as they act: find, place, check.

info.purpose: Hold the two files that outlast a run: {catalogue} and {contract}.

info.why: Tell how far {contract} is from fit for {reader}, one state at a time.

info.purpose: Draw one level as a graph with four parts.
Hold all levels together with three parts: one fixes items, one walks the graph, one constrains it.

nodes.label: Subject
nodes.purpose: Stand as the system, process or requirements that {reader} must rebuild.

nodes.label: Claude Code session
nodes.purpose: Host the skill where {subject}'s sources can be read.

info.goal: Rebuild {subject} with a recall of $\frac{a}{q}$ near one, where $a$ of the $q$ rebuild questions name the records that answer them.

nodes.label: Extraction run
nodes.purpose: Find, topic by topic, what {reader} needs to rebuild {subject}.

steps: list the sources and what each can settle
note each finding with where it was seen
info.why: a fixed topic list finds what a free reading skips: constants, wire formats, failure cases

nodes.label: Contract writing
nodes.purpose: Place each finding in the one slot of {contract} that {checker} and a page can read.

steps: name nodes as things and edges as sentences
draw each lifecycle as a region of states
run {checker}, read aloud, answer each open question

rows: the place and the rule are named, and no page is built until the slot is mended

nodes.label: Checker
nodes.purpose: Refuse {contract} while a page or {reader} could misread it, and list each open question.

nodes.label: Tag catalogue
nodes.purpose: Fix, per tag, the items worth recording and the form of each.

info.format: one JSON file: kind, tag, meaning, items with a form and an example

nodes.label: Contract
nodes.purpose: Hold all that is known of {subject} in one file that every later job reads.

rows: by hand or by a generator

nodes.label: Drafted contract
nodes.purpose: Mark {contract} as written and not yet accepted by {checker}.

nodes.label: Checked contract
nodes.purpose: Mark {contract} as one that {checker} printed `ok` for.

nodes.label: Answered contract
nodes.purpose: Mark {contract} as fit for {reader}: each open question is answered or recorded as a gap.

info.meaning: Every rebuild question is settled, by records that answer it or by a gap: $$\frac{1}{q}\sum_{i=1}^{q} s_i = 1, \quad s_i \in \{0, 1\}$$

nodes.label: Level
nodes.purpose: Show one depth of {subject}, small enough to read at once.

info.format: id, title, about, areas, nodes, edges

nodes.label: Area
nodes.purpose: Gather nodes for one reason, or hold the states of one thing.

nodes.label: Node
nodes.purpose: Name one thing of {subject}, or one state a thing can be in.

info.format: id, label, tag, area, opens, purpose, info, evidence

nodes.label: Edge
nodes.purpose: Join two nodes by one relation, or by one move between states.

info.format: from, to, label, tag, many, info, evidence

info.statement: {node}, {edge} or {area} holds only the items of its tag, each item in its form

nodes.label: Scenario
nodes.purpose: Show a purpose met, step by step, on the nodes and edges.

info.format: id, title, purpose, principle, steps of at, note

nodes.label: Property
nodes.purpose: State what must hold of the nodes and edges, what is assumed and what is not known.

info.format: id, kind, strength, status, fault, statement, on, paths

edges.label: sends its open questions back to

info.filter: only when a question is open

steps.note: prints ok, or names each break

scenarios.title: read-one-level
scenarios.purpose: {reader} tells the static sentences from the moves between states.

properties.title: one-file
properties.statement: Every page of {subject} is made from {contract} and nothing else.

properties.title: same-level
properties.statement: {node} sits in {area} of its own level: {node} and its area are drawn on one level.

properties.title: ids-once
properties.statement: An id is lowercase words joined by `-`, used once in the whole contract; the id of {edge} says what {edge} does and holds neither end's id, so moving an end leaves it true.

properties.title: sources-reachable
properties.statement: {subject}'s sources can be read by the session that extracts; what only a person knows must be asked.

properties.title: standard-library
properties.statement: {checker} uses the Python standard library only.

properties.title: sentence-truth
properties.statement: No script can tell whether a sentence is true of {subject}; only a reading of `read` against the sources can.

questions.asks: Who must be able to rebuild {subject}, and from what alone?
What is read to find the facts, and in what order of work?
Where does every fact end up, and which parts does that file hold?
What fixes the items a record of one tag must hold?
What does {checker} judge, and what does it send back?
Which states does a description pass through before it is done?
How is a record named so that another can point at it?
What does {checker} need installed to run?
How is a sentence of the description known to be true?
